title: Horizon and Gravity Again
premise: Coral Dunmore has kept Earth's abandoned seed vault alive for seven years, running cargo through orbits contested by the Meridian Combine and the Free Orbit League. When a manifest lists a ship that never flew — the Horizon's Grace — under her dead mother's name, Coral discovers her mother faked her death to seed a hidden archive at the edge of dead space. Racing a collapsing relay signal that will either broadcast the archive to everyone or destroy it forever, Coral must choose between protecting her mother's legacy and exposing the truth about who really abandoned Earth. In the end, Coral broadcasts everything — including her mother's confession — and chooses loyalty to truth over loyalty to blood.
about_author: Freya Thackeray is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. She lives in a coastal town where she keeps an obsessive garden and claims the sea sounds like re-entry.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghost
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Hauling cargo through contested orbit, she spots an impossible name on a routine manifest: the Horizon's Grace, a ship decommissioned before it ever flew — registered to her mother, dead seven years. The beat is quiet unease curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Dust
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present-tense vault maintenance. Coral remembers her mother Ilsa's final transmission and the sealed records she was told never to open. Emotional beat: grief that has calcified into duty.

chapters.title: The Buyer Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A Meridian Combine broker offers triple rate for a delivery to coordinates inside dead space — the same coordinates as the ghost ship's last logged ping. Beat: temptation sharpened by suspicion.

chapters.title: Vault Protocol
chapters.summary: POV of Wren, Coral's junior caretaker, who discovers someone accessed the vault's deep index remotely using Ilsa Dunmore's credentials. Beat: betrayal of the sanctuary Coral built.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Coral runs the gauntlet past a League patrol, nearly boarded. She learns both factions are hunting the Horizon's Grace signal. Beat: fear that she's already being watched.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Ledger
chapters.summary: Coral decrypts her mother's old cargo logs and finds seven years of falsified entries — shipments that never arrived anywhere. Beat: the first crack in the mother she mourned.

chapters.title: The Man from Meridian
chapters.summary: POV of Agent Sef Calloway, Combine intelligence, ordered to find whoever is chasing the Grace — and to make sure the archive never surfaces. Beat: cold professional dread; he suspects his own employers.

chapters.title: Dead Space Edge
chapters.summary: Coral and Wren jump toward the relay at the edge of dead space against protocol. The vault's systems begin failing behind them. Beat: point of no return, exhilaration laced with guilt.

chapters.title: Signal in the Static
chapters.summary: They intercept a fragment of the Grace's transmission: Ilsa's voice, reciting coordinates and one word — 'forgive.' Beat: Coral's composure shatters.

chapters.title: The Relay at Kestrel-9
chapters.summary: Arrival at the derelict relay station, half-eaten by micrometeorite scarring. Someone has been living aboard. Beat: eerie stillness, then evidence of recent life.

chapters.title: The Stowaway
chapters.summary: POV of Juno Reyes, a League defector hiding on the relay, who reveals the Grace never flew because its launch was sabotaged — by the Combine, with League complicity. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What the Vault Was For
chapters.summary: Juno explains Ilsa's plan: not seeds, but a full genomic and cultural archive proving Earth's abandonment was engineered, not inevitable. Beat: Coral's worldview upended.

chapters.title: Combine Interdiction
chapters.summary: Calloway's strike team hits the relay. Firefight in zero-g; Wren is wounded shielding the data core. Beat: terror, and Coral's first kill.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, drifting in and out of consciousness in medbay. They confess they tipped off the Combine weeks ago, believing Coral was compromised. Beat: shame and the fragile start of forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Grace Found
chapters.summary: Following Ilsa's coordinates, they locate the Horizon's Grace itself, adrift and intact, its holds packed with the archive. Beat: awe — standing inside a legend that was real all along.

chapters.title: Mother's Voice
chapters.summary: Aboard the Grace, Coral plays Ilsa's full log. Her mother confesses to falsifying her death, to abandoning Coral deliberately so no one would look for the archive through her. Beat: rage and heartbreak entwined.

chapters.title: Loyalty vs. Truth
chapters.summary: Juno argues for broadcasting everything; Wren begs Coral to bury it and save what's left of their lives. Beat: the thematic fault line made explicit, Coral silent at its center.

chapters.title: Calloway's Doubt
chapters.summary: Calloway's POV. His superiors order him to destroy the Grace with witnesses aboard. He stalls, digging into files he was never meant to see. Beat: a loyal man discovering his loyalty was purchased with lies.

chapters.title: The Relay Wakes
chapters.summary: The Kestrel-9 relay begins a countdown — Ilsa rigged it to auto-broadcast unless manually cancelled, or to burn out entirely if tampered with. Beat: the race becomes literal; time is now a character.

chapters.title: League Ambush
chapters.summary: A League squadron arrives demanding the archive as leverage against the Combine. Standoff aboard the Grace. Beat: Coral realizes every faction wants to own the truth, not free it.

chapters.title: Bargain in the Dark
chapters.summary: Coral negotiates passage and protection by promising the League exclusive access — a lie she hates herself for. Beat: moral compromise, hands shaking as she signs.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone cripples the Grace's drive. Evidence points to Wren again, but Coral finds traces of a Combine infiltrator among the League crew. Beat: paranoia; trust becomes a liability.

chapters.title: The Infiltrator
chapters.summary: Coral traps and confronts the Combine agent — a woman who once served under Ilsa and chose the Combine over her. Beat: mirror-scene; Coral sees the version of herself she could become.

chapters.title: Countdown: Forty Hours
chapters.summary: With the relay countdown accelerating, repairs race against the clock. Wren works through a fever. Beat: exhausted solidarity; the crew becomes a family of necessity.

chapters.title: Calloway Defects
chapters.summary: Calloway sends Coral the Combine's interdiction schedule and burns his career doing it. Beat: an enemy becoming an ally; the cost named plainly.

chapters.title: Dead Space Silence
chapters.summary: All comms go dark as the Combine jams the corridor. The crew is truly alone with the decision. Beat: claustrophobic hush before the storm.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Second Letter
chapters.summary: In the Grace's quarters, Coral finds a physical letter addressed 'To the child I chose to protect by leaving.' It asks her to decide freely, not obediently. Beat: the emotional keystone; forgiveness begins.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Coral puts the choice to the crew: broadcast, bury, or bargain. Each argues from wound and hope. Beat: democracy under pressure; Coral abstains, unable to speak.

chapters.title: Combine Assault
chapters.summary: The Combine fleet arrives early. Boarding action across the Grace's dark corridors; Juno is captured covering the retreat to the relay. Beat: sacrifice, chaos, rising dread.

chapters.title: Relay Interior
chapters.summary: Inside Kestrel-9's core, Coral reaches the manual override with minutes left. Calloway's intel proves the Combine will sterilize the whole sector afterward. Beat: the trap within the trap revealed.

chapters.title: Thirty Seconds
chapters.summary: Coral's hand on the cancel switch. Flashbacks of Ilsa, of the vault, of Wren bleeding. Beat: the novel's held breath — she lets the countdown run.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: The relay fires the archive across every open channel: the engineered abandonment, the Combine's crimes, Ilsa's confession, and Coral's own name attached as witness. Beat: catharsis and irrevocability at once.

chapters.title: Aftermath: The Fleet Scatters
chapters.summary: The Combine's cover collapses; League commanders implicated too. The assault falters as crews mutiny rather than fire on the messenger. Beat: vindication without triumph.

chapters.title: Rescue and Reckoning
chapters.summary: Calloway extracts Juno; Wren's survival is confirmed. Coral faces the crew she lied to and confesses her bargain with the League. Beat: honesty as repair.

chapters.title: Return to the Vault
chapters.summary: Coral comes home to the seed vault, half-failing, and chooses to rebuild it — not as a shrine to the past but as a living archive, open to all. Beat: inheritance reclaimed on her own terms.

chapters.title: The Trial of Names
chapters.summary: Months later, Coral testifies via relay before a joint tribunal, refusing to soften Ilsa's record or her own compromises. Beat: accountability as the truest form of love.

chapters.title: Letters to Dead Space
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude: Coral writes letters to her mother she'll never send, and finally sends one anyway, addressed to the relay. Beat: mourning completed, memory transformed.

chapters.title: New Manifests
chapters.summary: Ships begin arriving at the vault voluntarily — settlers, archivists, defectors. Wren takes over logistics; Coral trains successors. Beat: the lonely watch becomes a community.

chapters.title: Horizon and Gravity
chapters.summary: Coral flies the restored Horizon's Grace on its first true voyage, scattering memorial beacons along Ilsa's route. Beat: reconciliation with the dead, gravity finally released.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Coral's POV at the vault's observation deck. The archive travels outward on a thousand ships; the truth belongs to everyone now. She plants a seed her mother catalogued and watches it take root. Beat: peace earned, legacy chosen.
